Software Update

Update SATOM's own code and Python dependencies — from the git remote or from a signed offline package — through a privileged runner, standby first on a pair.

👤 ForAdministratorAdvanced user
🔑 Permissionsusers.manage
📍 WhereSettings → System → Software Update (URL /self-update/)

What is it?#

Software Update updates SATOM itself: the application code and its Python dependencies, never operating-system packages. There are two delivery paths — from the git remote (check, then apply) and from a signed offline package for nodes with no route to the remote. In both cases the web application only enqueues a request; a separate privileged runner performs the update, restarts the service, health-checks it and rolls back automatically if the check fails.

What does it do?#

  • Shows this node: host name, role (PRIMARY, STANDBY or role: unknown) and the running revision and branch.
  • Check for updates fetches the configured branch from the git remote and lists the commits this node is behind.
  • Apply update queues an update to that revision, optionally with pip install -r requirements.txt and flask db upgrade.
  • Enforces the staged-rollout safeguard on a pair: the primary can only take a revision the standby has already applied and validated.
  • Deploy automation switches the reconciler between Manual (observe only) and Auto (drives the staged rollout by itself).
  • Shows the live progress of a running update and the Recent updates history with a per-step log.
  • Offline update package: shows the trust store, checks the public release feed for a newer package, downloads or uploads a package into staging, runs a preflight, and applies it.
  • Knowledge packs (3.0): shows the pack installed per lane (API pack, knowledge pack) with its age, checks the knowledge feed, downloads and imports the rolling knowledge pack, and sets the daily fetch mode — see Knowledge packs.
  • API library packs: lists, uploads and imports signed packs item by item — the release's own API pack and any uploaded pack (see API library). Packs are verified with the keys of their lane, not with the update trust store (Pack trust).

Requirements#

  • users.manage and the Global ADOM.
  • The privileged runner installed and enabled on the node: the systemd path unit satom-updater.path watches the request queue and starts satom-updater.service (see Services and timers).
  • Git path: the code remote configured in Settings → Software Update Repository and reachable from the node.
  • Offline path: at least one public key in the node's trust store, installed as root with satom execute trust add-key <file.pub>.
  • Neither the git update path nor an offline package can be applied on a container installation; there the release is switched from Container operations.

Permissions#

Every route on the page requires users.manage (legacy coarse key user_manage); in the default profiles only Administrator has it.

🔑Permission

Without users.manage the Administrator menu is hidden and /self-update/ returns 403 Forbidden.

Role-based restrictions on a pair:

  • Deploy automation is a replicated setting: the Save button is disabled on the standby (Change automation on the PRIMARY node — this node's database is read-only).
  • Apply update to PRIMARY stays disabled until the standby has validated a revision (see below).
  • API pack import is refused on the standby.

How to use#

Update from the git remote#

  1. Open Settings → System → Software Update.
  2. In This node, click Check for updates. The Available update card shows either Up to date on <commit> or N new commit(s) available — target <commit> with the commit list.
  3. Leave Update Python dependencies and Run DB migrations ticked unless you have a reason not to.
  4. Click Apply update to this node (on a standby or a single node) or Apply update to PRIMARY.
  5. The flash reads Update queued (<id>). The privileged runner is applying it — watch the live status below. The service will restart mid-update. The Update in progress panel shows each step as it finishes and what is running now; during the restart it says it is reconnecting.
  6. When the state becomes success or failed, the page reloads and the run appears in Recent updates. Click log to see every step.
  1. 1Check for updatesgit fetch of the configured branch
  2. 2Applythe page writes a request file — nothing privileged yet
  3. 3Runner startssatom-updater.path sees the request, starts satom-updater.service
  4. 4Snapshot + checkoutcurrent commit recorded; local commits parked first
  5. 5pip + migrationsper the two tick boxes (migrations on the primary only)
  6. 6Restart + health check200 from /healthz within the timeout
  7. 7Success or rollbacka failed step resets to the snapshot and restarts

Update a pair (standby first)#

  1. Open the page on the standby and apply the update there. On a standby the runner updates the code, skips migrations (the schema arrives by replication), validates the result and writes a validated marker into the primary's database.
  2. Open the page on the primary. The Available update card now shows Standby validated <commit> — the primary is cleared to update. Apply.

If you try the primary first, the button is disabled with Safeguard active. and, if submitted anyway, the flash reads Blocked by the staged-rollout safeguard: update the STANDBY to this revision and let it pass its health check first, then the PRIMARY unlocks. In standalone mode (see High Availability) the safeguard is off.

Let the reconciler deploy automatically#

  1. On the primary, in Deploy automation, choose Auto — reconciler deploys (standby first, then primary) and click Save.
  2. The reconciler (satom-reconciler, running on both nodes) checks the remote every 60 seconds. When behind, it updates the standby first and the primary only after the standby has validated the same revision. After a failed update it backs off for 15 minutes.
  3. Reconciler last tick shows its latest decision (for example observe, up-to-date, enqueued-standby, await-standby, cooldown). In Recent updates its runs carry the auto origin badge.

Choose Manual — I apply updates by hand to make the reconciler observe and log only.

Apply an offline update package#

  1. In Offline update package, check the Trust store line. With no key installed, every package is refused.
  2. Get the package in one of two ways: - Click Check for a newer package online. If a newer version exists, click Download & stage; it downloads as a background job and then opens its preflight. The message names the feed it read: the public one by default, or the internal pipeline set in General → Update sources, with its user and token if it needs them. The signature check does not change with the source. - Or choose a file under Upload satom-update-<version>.tar.gz and click Upload & check.
  3. Select the staged package. The Preflight table lists every check with ok, warn or fail.
  4. If the package is older than the running version, tick I understand this is a downgrade.
  5. Click Apply package to this node. A database backup is taken first (on the primary), the service restarts, and a failed health check rolls the node back.

❗Important

On a pair, stage the package on the primary and apply on each node — the standby first. A file uploaded on the standby is removed by the next data sync. Package build, signing and key management are covered in Offline updates.

Import an API library pack#

Select a pack under Available packs (or upload satom-apipack-<version>.tar.gz), tick the new and update items and click Import selected. The import runs as a job. Do it on the primary. Details: API library.

Keep the knowledge current#

Use the Knowledge packs card: Check now, Import, and the Scheduled fetch (daily) mode. An update to 3.3.2 or later creates the daily action by itself when the node comes from 2.x; going to an older 3.x, create it once with sudo satom execute seed actions --yes. Details: Knowledge packs; what 3.0 changes: Upgrading to 3.0.

Sign releases (optional enforcement)#

A node can pin what the root runner installs from deploy/ (unit files, install-*.sh scripts, the operator CLI, the runner copies) to a release an operator signed. Enforcement is off until a root-owned trust anchor, /etc/satom/release-trust.allowed_signers (or a single key at /etc/satom/release-trust.pub), is installed on the node; install it on both nodes of a pair. With the anchor in place:

The update's target Result
is a signed commit root-side content is installed from it
is unsigned, deploy/ identical to its newest signed ancestor root-side content is installed from that signed ancestor
is unsigned and deploy/ changed since the last signed release the application updates; the root-side refresh is held and the update shows a warning step

To sign, on the primary as root run sudo satom execute sign-release (dry run), then sudo satom execute sign-release --yes; satom get release trust shows where the node stands. To turn enforcement off, remove the anchor on both nodes. Details: Security model.

Configuration#

Field Description Required Example
Update Python dependencies Runs pip install -r requirements.txt during a git update. Ticked by default. No ticked
Run DB migrations Runs flask db upgrade during a git update (skipped on a standby). Ticked by default. No ticked
Deploy automation Manual (default) or Auto. Replicated; set on the primary. No Manual
Package file A file named like satom-update-<version>.tar.gz (letters, digits, . _ -), at most 400 MB. The 5 newest staged packages are kept. Yes (upload) satom-update-2.10.1.tar.gz
I understand this is a downgrade Required to apply a package older than the running version. Only for downgrades ticked

The branch that is checked comes from the environment variable FM_UPDATE_BRANCH (default main); the remote itself is set in Settings.

Preflight checks#

Check Fails when
Trust store the trust store has a problem or holds no key
Archive the file cannot be extracted cleanly
Signature & integrity the signature does not verify against a trusted key, or files do not match the signed manifest
Version the version cannot be compared (an older version is a warn, the same version a warn)
Upgrade path the node is older than the package's minimum starting version (from 3.3.4: 3.3.3 — a node on 3.3.2 or older applies satom-update-3.3.3.tar.gz first)
Python the package's wheels do not match the node's Python
Dependencies a pinned dependency change has no wheel in the package
Disk space free space is below about three times the package size (warn below six times)
This node never fails; warn on a standby

Example#

🧪Example — Two-node update from the remote

An administrator opens Software Update on the standby, clicks Check for updates (3 new commits), and clicks Apply update to this node. The steps show snapshot current commit, git fetch origin main, checkout …, pip install -r requirements.txt, flask db upgrade — skipped (standby; schema via replication), restart services, health check, route audit and mark validated on primary. On the primary the card now reads Standby validated …; she applies there and the run finishes with postflight (after).

Result#

  • Each run writes a status record and appears in Recent updates (the last 15 runs on this node) with node, role, target, result and step log. A failed run shows failed · rolled back.
  • A successful standby run unlocks the primary for that exact revision.
  • Offline package uploads, deletions, downloads and applies are recorded in the Audit Log (update_package.upload, update_package.delete, update_package.download, update_package.apply), as are API pack actions, queued git updates and deploy-automation (reconciler) mode changes.

ℹ️Note

Changed in 2.11.0: applying a git update and changing the deploy-automation mode write Audit Log entries, an offline package is refused with the reason on a container installation, and an update installs a satom.service that binds the application server to 127.0.0.1:8000 only — an update no longer re-opens port 8000 on all interfaces.

Troubleshooting#

After updating from 2.x, Script Library runs stay queued or the SQL console refuses queries#

Possible causes - The node was updated by its 2.x runner to a release older than 3.3.2. That runner does not know the units and the database role 3.x added, so it did not install the Script Library's satom-scripts.path nor the console's read-only role, and it created none of the 3.x scheduled actions.

Solution 1. Update the node to 3.3.2 or later. Its refresh update runner step finishes the job (units, console role, the 3.x scheduled actions, once) and warns about what it could not do. 2. Or by hand, on the primary: sudo satom execute reinstall units, sudo bash /opt/satom/deploy/install-console-role.sh, sudo satom execute seed actions --yes. 3. The Script Library also needs bubblewrap: install it under Settings → General → System packages if the step warns about it.

Verification - systemctl is-enabled satom-scripts.path says enabled, a SQL console query runs, and sudo satom execute seed actions reports already armed.

The update shows "root-side refresh held"#

Possible causes - A release trust anchor is installed, and deploy/ changed since the last signed release. The application code was updated; the unit files, install scripts, operator CLI and runner copies were not.

Solution 1. On the primary, run sudo satom execute sign-release and review the deploy/ diff it shows. 2. Run sudo satom execute sign-release --yes. 3. Update again (standby first, then primary).

Verification - sudo satom get release trust reports that HEAD's deploy/ matches the newest signed commit, and the next update has no held step.

Update stays "queued" — "still queued: check that satom-updater.path is enabled on this node."#

Possible causes - The satom-updater.path unit is disabled or stopped, so nothing picks up the request.

Solution 1. Enable and start satom-updater.path on this node.

Verification - The panel switches to Running: … within seconds.

"Blocked by the staged-rollout safeguard: …"#

Possible causes - This is the primary of a pair and the standby has not validated this exact revision.

Solution 1. Apply the same update on the standby and wait for success. 2. Return to the primary and apply.

Verification - Standby validated <commit> — the primary is cleared to update.

"Fetch error: …" after Check for updates#

Possible causes - The git remote is unreachable or its credentials are wrong.

Solution 1. Check Settings → Software Update Repository. 2. If the node cannot reach the remote at all, use an offline package.

"Refused: this package still fails preflight (…). Nothing was applied."#

Possible causes - At least one preflight check is fail (listed in the parentheses).

Solution 1. Select the package and read the failing row. For Trust store, install the release key: satom execute trust add-key <key.pub>.

Verification - Every row is ok or warn and Apply package to this node is enabled.

"Upload rejected: …"#

Possible causes - The file name does not look like satom-update-<version>.tar.gz, the file is empty, or it exceeds the 400 MB limit.

Solution 1. Upload the package file exactly as published, without renaming it.

"This package is OLDER than the running version. …"#

Solution 1. Tick I understand this is a downgrade and apply again. Migrations are not reversed; keep the database backup the apply takes.

Update finished "failed · rolled back"#

Possible causes - A step failed (fetch, pip, migration, health check, route audit).

Solution 1. Open the log of the run and find the first red step. 2. If the rollback step says STILL UNHEALTHY after rollback, check the service on the node before retrying.

A message about the container runtime#

On a container install the git updater, offline packages and code rollback on System backup are unavailable by design: the code is part of the image. The flash names the alternative. Use Container operations.

Advanced#

Advanced The privileged runner
  • The web process runs unprivileged and cannot restart itself. A request is a JSON file written atomically into data/update-requests/. The satom-updater.path unit (DirectoryNotEmpty) starts the one-shot satom-updater.service, which runs as root with a 30-minute start timeout, removes the request and works through it. Progress goes to data/update-status/<id>.json, which the page polls.
  • The same queue carries other kinds of request: offline packages, single-library pip changes from Settings, service actions, and HA promotion.
  • Before resetting the checkout, commits that exist only locally are parked under refs/backup/; if that fails the update aborts.
  • The health check waits for HTTP 200 from /healthz (90 seconds by default). A node whose web service was not running before the update gets an import smoke test instead.
  • Unit files shipped in deploy/ and the operator CLI are refreshed on every update; the node's enabled/disabled state is not changed. With a release trust anchor installed, this root-side content comes only from a signed release — see Sign releases.
Advanced What is node-local

The virtual environment, staged packages and update history are per node. Apply on each node of a pair and confirm with satom diagnose updates and satom diagnose code.
